### Sushil Suri v. CBI (2011)

The Supreme Court laid down that fraud is an essential ingredient of forgery under Section 463. Without establishing fraudulent intent, no conviction can be recorded under the forgery provisions. This case remains the foundational judicial authority on what must be proven to establish forgery.

### Sheila Sebastian v. R. Jawaharaj (2018)

The Supreme Court held that liability for forgery cannot be imposed on someone who is not the actual maker of the false document. In this case, a Power of Attorney was allegedly created by impersonating the property owner. The court held that all ingredients of both Sections 463 and 464 must be satisfied before a conviction under Section 465 can be recorded – neither section operates independently.
